key_insight: The study shows that optimized metallic microstructure and texture can be used to infer the likely alloy composition and processing recipe, but conventional, physics-inspired descriptors outperform learned embeddings on this small dataset.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical reverse-design route for alloy development, where measured microstructure can help recover plausible extrusion settings and alloy choices when expert intuition is limited.
method: Dataset: 107 magnesium alloy extrusion conditions from 14 alloys, with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three descriptors: conventional grain/texture statistics, a pretrained vision embedding, and a graph neural network on the grain network.
Two prediction tasks: infer alloy composition from process conditions, and infer process parameters from composition and microstructure/texture.
evidence_signal: In 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy in 65% of held-out cases versus 17% for majority-class guessing, while learned embeddings stayed below 30%; microstructure roughly halved temperature error in process inference.
watch_item: The dataset is small and the targets are effectively discrete because only a limited set of alloys and extrusion settings were used, so generalization beyond the known recipe space may be limited.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
